props.title: Horror of Dracula

sections.content: Horror of Dracula (1958) revolutionized vampire cinema through Christopher Lee's commanding performance and Hammer Films' vivid Technicolor gore. Unlike the gothic shadows of Nosferatu (1922) and Universal's Dracula (1931), Hammer's interpretation explodes with crimson blood and Lee's imposing 6'5" frame. Director Terence Fisher transforms Bram Stoker's novel into a fast-paced thriller, while Peter Cushing's Van Helsing brings scientific precision to vampire hunting. The film's saturated colors and overt sexuality broke new ground, influencing everything from Interview with the Vampire (1994) to Bram Stoker's Dracula (1992).

sections.content: Hammer Films transformed horror cinema in the late 1950s by reimagining Universal's monster classics in lurid color. The Curse of Frankenstein (1957) proved the formula, but Horror of Dracula perfected it. The studio's approach emphasized blood, cleavage, and religious imagery, creating a distinctly British horror style that influenced generations of filmmakers. The Lee-Cushing dynamic would be repeated in numerous Hammer productions, including The Mummy (1959) and The Hound of the Baskervilles (1959).

The film's climactic confrontation between Dracula and Van Helsing set new standards for horror movie showdowns. The innovative use of sunlight, crosses, and physical combat created a template still followed today in films like Blade (1998) and Van Helsing (2004). Fisher's direction keeps the action taught while never losing the gothic atmosphere that made Hammer famous. SUBHEAD: Legacy and Influence

sections.content: Christopher Lee's interpretation of Dracula became definitive, inspiring countless imitators. His sophisticated menace and physical presence influenced performances from Gary Oldman in Bram Stoker's Dracula (1992) to Luke Evans in Dracula Untold (2014). The film's success launched a series of Dracula sequels, though Lee grew increasingly frustrated with the diminishing quality, making his final appearance in The Satanic Rites of Dracula (1973).
